scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Parachicos of Chiapa de Corzo
This is Parachico. 17th century.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The tradition dates to the 17th century, coinciding with the construction of the church and the arrival of the image of Saint Sebastian.
It is considered a hybrid of pre-Hispanic indigenous roots and Spanish Catholic influence.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is a ritual offering held during the Grand Fiesta of Chiapa de Corzo, honoring the Black Christ of Esquipulas, Saint Anthony Abbot, and Saint Sebastian.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers move through the streets of the town, visiting churches and private homes.
They perform for the saints, often stopping to touch the images, cross themselves, and offer thanks.
The group is led by a patrón.
on_screen: Formation: Processional movement through town streets and visits to specific homes and churches
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is performed to the sound of a drum and a reed flute, locally called a pito.
Dancers also chant and improvise verses during the procession.
Listen for the Drum, Reed flute (pito).
The music is driven by the rhythmic shaking of metallic rattles combined with the melodic accompaniment of a reed flute and a drum.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear wooden masks with Caucasian features, round headdresses, colorful ribbons, striped serapes, and embroidered shawls over dark clothing.
They carry chinchines (rattles).
